text_blocks.snippet: Hilliard Law is representing consumers in legal action against Intuit, the maker of TurboTax, for alleged privacy violations. The firm is investigating whether TurboTax employed tracking tools that shared user data without consent, potentially violating California privacy laws. This investigation is part of a broader effort to hold Intuit accountable for its tax preparation services.
snippet_highlighted_words: representing consumers in legal action against Intuit, the maker of TurboTax, for alleged privacy violations

list.title: Privacy Violations:
list.snippet: Hilliard Law is looking into claims that Intuit used tracking tools on its website to collect and share user data without proper consent.

list.title: Target Audience:
list.snippet: The firm is specifically seeking California residents who used TurboTax's online tax filing services.

list.title: Legal Action:
list.snippet: Hilliard Law is exploring potential legal recourse, including arbitration, for consumers who believe their privacy rights were violated by Intuit.

list.title: Settlement and Distribution:
list.snippet: A separate $141 million multistate settlement was reached with Intuit for consumers who were misled into paying for what should have been free tax services. Consumers eligible for payments from this settlement were notified automatically and did not need to file a claim.

list.title: FTC Ruling:
list.snippet: The FTC also found Intuit engaged in deceptive advertising practices regarding "free" TurboTax services.
